title: The Egg - A Short Story
beats: You die in an ordinary accident and meet the narrator
Afterlife void; he claims to be God; you worry about your family
Narrator is plain and vague; your family will be fine, with a bitter detail
You expect Heaven or Hell; told reincarnation instead
Blank slate assumption is corrected: all past experience is in you
Finger in a glass of water: part of you enters a human and brings back the experience
Many lives; next you are a Chinese peasant girl in 540 AD, so time is not linear
Narrator says the origin is beyond your understanding
You may have met yourself in other lives
Purpose of the universe: you maturing, and only you
Chain of you are Lincoln and Booth, Hitler and victims, Jesus and followers
Harming others is harming yourself; every experience is yours
You will become like God; you are a fetus
The universe is an egg; sent on to next life

metrics.misconception: yes: blank slate / heaven or hell / many people exist
metrics.examples: 1 analogy (water glass), 4 identity reveals escalating in moral weight
metrics.ending: Egg metaphor named by the viewer, then the narrator sends you on

principles.1: confirmed: your own death and family 0:03-1:09
principles.5: confirmed: you literally are the character 0:03
principles.7: confirmed: viewer-character states Wait, I'm everyone 5:40 before narrator confirms
principles.8: partly: dialogue pace flat; reveals escalate slowly in beats
principles.11: confirmed: reincarnation before everyone-is-you before purpose

new_moves.name: character-voices-the-objection
new_moves.what: The second-person character asks the viewer's likely questions, so the narrator answers in dialogue

new_moves.name: escalating-reveal-chain
new_moves.what: Repeat the same identity move with higher-stakes cases until the implication lands

new_moves.name: learner-states-the-insight
new_moves.what: The learner voices the conclusion, the narrator only confirms

theory: The learner is cast as the protagonist, who asks each natural question in turn, so every answer corrects an assumption just voiced. The central insight comes from repeated, escalating instances until you say it yourself. The metaphor title is withheld until the viewer names it.
velocity: Learner model: have the tutor voice likely misconceptions as a character line, then correct
Scene builder: escalating example chain, same structure, rising stakes, with a final learner-stated rule
Evals: check whether the learner states the generalization before the tutor does
Orchestrator: reserve the metaphor label (the egg) for the last beat
quote: Wait... I'm... everyone? Now you're getting it.
